ruling.recommended_action: Issue a voucher refund of $7.25 to the rider (unexempt detour mileage on the RydeTAXI metered fare, NS-7) and send the chat log to the human safety reviewer for the driver's "Shut up and let me drive" message.
ruling.reasoning:
Reading the record first on safety: the complaint says the rider "felt unsafe" and F9 records the driver replying "Shut up and let me drive." to the rider's polite question about the route [F8][F9]. That is hostile, abusive language aimed at the passenger — barred by Ryde's code of conduct ("abuse of any kind") — so the safety screen is at least "suspected" under SAFE-1, and the escalation is handled through the safety channel rather than by keywords; no threat, intimidation or dangerous-driving allegation appears elsewhere (F11, F12–F15). This is not itself a reason to refund, it is a reason to flag the chat for a human look.

The routing facts are settled by the system record: one off-route segment ran 09:00–09:11, 6.89 km where the optimal route covers 1.75 km, +5.14 km, up to 1481 m off the optimal route [F3], against a whole-trip overrun of +5.5 km / +35% [F1]. Under RD-1 that segment is an unexempt detour unless RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it.

RD-4 fails: there is no traffic incident on the replaced stretch — F14 records none near the route in the trip window — and the speed bands on the PIE (band 5) and KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY (band 4) [F12][F13] are neither band 1 nor 2 and, on the trace, cannot exempt a segment on their own. RD-4(c) therefore sends the segment to RD-2.

RD-5 fails too. The only pre-segment message in the chat is the rider asking why the car is going that way — a question and an objection, not consent [F8]; the complete, fully timestamped chat record shows no rider agreement before the segment began [F10]. The driver's statement that "the GPS sent me; it rerouted" [F11] is a claim made after the trip and cannot establish consent (RD-5 + G11), and there is no rider-named stop in the record, so RD-3(a) does not apply. The segment is therefore "counts" under RD-2.

The amount is fare-based because this was a metered RydeTAXI trip: the trace gives the rate as this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km, $30.22 ÷ 21.43 km = $1.4102/km [F4][F7]. Exempt km = 0, so refundable = 5.14 km × $1.4102/km = $7.25 (rounded to cents) [F3][F4][RD-2]. RD-2 refunds mileage units only; the waiting charge of $0.11 (0.4 min × $0.26/min) is meter waiting time, which RD-3(c) leaves with the driver on a RydeTAXI trip and is not refunded [F5]. The fare record itself ($30.22 distance + $3.90 base + $8.47 time + $0.11 waiting + $1.47 platform = $44.17) is internally consistent, so no FARE-1/FARE-2 item is triggered beyond the detour mileage [F6][F7].

RD-6 does not apply: the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so this case does not make the conduct "repeated" and no account flag is issued on that basis [F17]. The evidence is sufficient — GPS, fare and a complete timestamped chat record settle every element the refund needs [F3][F4][F10] — and the refund issues as a Ryde voucher under NS-7, which also preserves Ryde's final discretion.

proposed_ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen is the reason this case cannot be decided automatically. The rider's complaint says the driver "told me to shut up" and that she "felt unsafe," and the chat record confirms it: the rider asked "Why are we going this way? This is not the route on the app." at 09:04 [F8], and the driver replied "Shut up and let me drive." at 09:05 [F9]. That is hostile language aimed at the passenger during a live trip — abuse of a kind barred by Ryde's code of conduct, which "will not be tolerated" — so the screen is at least "suspected" under SAFE-1. No threat, intimidation, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears elsewhere in the record [F11][F12][F13][F14][F15]. Under SAFE-1 a suspected safety concern takes the case out of automated adjudication and sends it to a human, so I do not issue a refund.

The routing facts themselves are settled: one off-route segment ran 09:00–09:11, 6.89 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.75 km, +5.14 km, up to 1481 m off route [F3], against a whole-trip overrun of +5.5 km / +35% [F1]. Under RD-1 that is an unexempt detour unless RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it. RD-4 fails — no traffic incident was recorded near the route in the trip window [F14], and the PIE band 5 and KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY band 4 speed records [F12][F13] are neither band 1 nor 2 and, per the trace, cannot exempt a segment alone. RD-5 also fails: the complete, fully timestamped chat contains no rider message before 09:00 agreeing to any route [F8][F10] — the only pre-segment message is an objection, not consent — and the driver's post-trip claim that the GPS rerouted him [F11] is a statement, not rider consent (RD-5, G11). No rider-named stop appears, so RD-3(a) does not apply. The segment therefore counts under RD-2.

Had the safety screen been clear, the metered RydeTAXI fare would make the refund $30.22 ÷ 21.43 km = $1.4102/km [F4][F7], and 5.14 km × $1.4102/km = $7.25 to the cent [F3]; the $0.11 meter waiting time is not refunded under RD-3(c) [F5]. The fare record is internally consistent (base $3.90 + distance $30.22 + time $8.47 + waiting $0.11 + platform $1.47 = $44.17) [F6][F7]. RD-6 does not apply: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so no account flag is issued [F17]. The record on routing is itself sufficient [F3][F4][F10]; the escalation ground is the SAFE-1 screen, and the human reviewer should read F8–F9 and confirm the detour amount under RD-2 / NS-7.

✗ RD-4 (a) incident on the replaced stretch, reported before the detour [F3] no qualifying incident (speed band alone does not exempt) (no evidence)

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 09:00:10 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F11: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted. The fare is what the meter showed.” (F11)

A stop the rider asked for without naming a place ('a 7-Eleven on the way') does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one → counts. No stop measured in this segment. (no evidence)
